Giovanni Wenzler.b:
Giovanni Wenzler became an Assistant Coach after graduating from UC Santa Cruz in 2022. During his collegiate swimming career, he helped the UC Santa Cruz Swim & Dive Team win their first Pacific Collegiate Swimming Conference title in 2020, and place 2nd in 2019 and 2022. His specialties are in butterfly and distance, with a focus on underwaters, and his best event being the 200 Fly.
In his first year as an assistant coach, he helped lead the Banana Slug men to 2nd place and women to 5th place in PCSC.
As a coach, he looks forward to fostering growth in his student-athletes, and giving new and returning swimmers the same positive and rewarding experience he got as a Banana Slug.

Hailey Garlich.b:
Hailey Garlich joined the UC Santa Cruz Banana Slugs in 2023, beginning her tenure as the Associate Head Coach for both men's and women's swim and dive.
Garlich is a former swimmer for Division II Grand Valley State University in Michigan, specializing in the Backstroke and Individual Medleys. After her collegiate swimming journey, she became a Graduate Assistant Coach at the University of South Dakota. During her three years at USD, Garlich helped guide the Distance and IM swimmers to numerous top 8 finishes and broken school records at the Summit League Conference Championships. She also helped lead the Coyotes to their first-ever conference title with the men becoming the 2021 Summit League Champions.
Garlich then made her way to Utah Tech University to help guide the Trailblazer women to their most outstanding season to date. The Trailblazers had 4 women qualify for and swim at the 2023 US Open. They also broke every school record, earned multiple top 3 finishes, and had one swimmer earn Swimmer of the Year all at the Western Athletic Conference Championships. The Utah Tech team also finished the season with the third best percentage of lifetime best swims in all of Division I.

Matthew Crawford.b:
Matt Crawford was promoted to Head Coach of the men’s and women’s swimming and diving teams in June 2019 after serving as the interim head coach for six months.
Crawford had been interim head coach since January 2019, his first year in the program after being hired as the Associate Head Coach for the Banana Slugs in August 2018.
"I believe Matt has the experience, proven leadership capacity and ability to foster a culture of compliance and success for the future of our men's and women's swimming and diving program," said Director of Athletics Susan Harriman.
He led the Banana Slugs to their best combined showing in years at the 2019 Pacific Collegiate Swimming Conference meet. The men placed second and the women were ninth. In addition, diver Ethan Johnson qualified for the NCAA Regionals in Iowa. In 2020, the Banana Slug men won their first PCSC title in school history and Crawford was named Conference men's coach of the year.
Crawford, a former UC Davis swimmer, was coach for the Davis Aquamonsters and Elk Grove Aquatics Club before coming to Santa Cruz.

Ariel Rittenhouse OLY.b:
Ariel Rittenhouse joined the UC Santa Cruz staff as a Volunteer Assistant in 2022 before being named Diving Coach in Fall 2023.
Coach Rittenhouse is a 2008 Beijing Olympic team member for the sport of diving. A Santa Cruz native who began diving at the age of 7, she is a two-time world cup medalist, a two-time World Championship team member, and a 2007 Pan American Games Silver Medalist. She placed fourth in the 2008 Beijing Olympics in the women’s three meter synchronized diving event with her diving partner, Kelci Bryant.
Coach Rittenhouse attended college at Florida State University, and held the school record in the women’s three meter after her gold medal winning performance at the 2013 ACC Championships. In 2013 she was named the diver of the year and was the Golden Nole Award winner at Florida State.
From 2016-2020, Coach Rittenhouse was elected to the US Olympic and Paralympic Committee’s Athlete Advisory Council and represented the diving athlete population along with serving on USA Diving’s Board of Directors.
Coach Rittenhouse comes from a family of Olympians, with her mother, Sharon Rittenhouse, earning a silver medal in the 400 I.M. at the 1964 Olympic Games, and her uncle, Michael Finneran, competing in diving at the 1972 Olympic Games.
